reads.what_it_sells: A hosted platform where you define an AI agent (prompt, model, guardrails) as a config object that gets its own API endpoint, a spend cap set on the key itself, and automatic logging of every call's tokens/latency/model — replacing the manual cost-tracking and per-provider dashboard aggregation we currently do by hand.
reads.relevance_feedback: The email's central claim — that usage keyed to the API key holder tells you who spent but not which agent spent, and that retry loops/session tables/spend sheets get built reactively after an incident — matches the profile almost exactly: we run multiple agents across providers in production, have had past incidents, and already do weekly per-agent cost reporting by hand. This isn't a generic pain point guess; it's the specific gap our current reporting job has.
assumed_experiences: Has had an incident traced back to missing per-agent cost or usage visibility
Currently aggregates spend by pulling CSVs from multiple provider dashboards into a hand-built spend sheet
Tracks usage keyed to whoever holds the provider API key rather than to the calling agent
Has built retry logic and session/run tracking reactively, after something broke
reads.problem_now: Live, current problem per the profile: weekly per-agent cost reporting already exists as a recurring task, and past incidents are named explicitly — this isn't a hypothetical future risk, it's the thing the team does every week and has already been burned by.
reads.biggest_doubt: This asks us to route production agent traffic through a new third-party hosted endpoint. "orqAgent is a hosted layer where an agent is a configuration object" — doesn't say which providers/models are behind it, which is the first thing an existing multi-provider shop needs to know.
